title: EEG and autonomic responses during emotional word association

affiliations.name: Tecnologico de Monterrey, School of Humanities and Education

description: This dataset comprises synchronized electroencephalographic and autonomic physiological recordings acquired during an emotional word association task focused on fear-related concepts. Participants generated or selected words in response to emotionally relevant lexical prompts while EEG (8 channels, 250 Hz), electrodermal activity, blood volume pulse, interbeat interval, and skin temperature were continuously recorded. The dataset includes behavioral event markers with semantic similarity measures between consecutive words, enabling investigation of neural and physiological correlates of emotional semantic processing.
methods_description: EEG signals were acquired using an OpenBCI Cyton board with Ultracortex Mark IV headset (8 channels: Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, P7, P8, O1, O2; sampling rate 250 Hz). Autonomic physiological signals (electrodermal activity, blood volume pulse, interbeat interval, skin temperature) were recorded using an Empatica E4 wristband. Participants completed a word association task lasting approximately three minutes, during which they either selected suggested words or generated novel words in response to emotionally relevant prompts. All data streams were timestamped during acquisition to enable synchronization.
